verdict.rationale: Firebase Security Rules are explicitly documented as a mechanism to define per-user, per-document data access control across Firestore, Realtime Database, and Cloud Storage, enforced server-side outside the app (firebase-docs-10, firebase-docs-18, firebase-docs-34). Community commentary corroborates that this authorization model works well in practice, allowing developers to separate data access logic from enforcement (firebase-comm-6), though some found storage rules cumbersome to reimplement when migrating providers (firebase-comm-9), which is a portability gripe not a functional failure. Missing for 10: a concrete row-level example (e.g., a rule restricting document access to its owning user) and independent hands-on validation of complex rule scenarios.
